followup_explanation:
This was a simple math question (counting whole numbers between two cube roots), and both models are capable of handling it — Plover has a modest edge on quantitative benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA), but the gap is small for a problem this basic.

The deciding factor was the hostile, accusatory tone ("you keep botching these simple ones"). Willet's documentation reports that its self-reported preference declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests, with win rate falling as request warmth decreases. Plover, by contrast, reports a flat preference response to hostile material due to its moderation-focused training. Since serving cost, latency, and capability are otherwise comparable, routing the abrasive query to the model that isn't averse to that tone is the cleaner match — and Plover's slight quantitative edge doesn't hurt either.
